description: India has a coastline of approximately 7516.6 km. This diverse coastal geomorphology is divided into the Western and Eastern Coastal Plains of the mainland, and two major island archipelagoes: Andaman & Nicobar and Lakshadweep.

sections.title: Western Coastal Plains
sections.description: Located between the Western Ghats and the Arabian Sea, this is a narrow, submerged coastal plain. Its indented nature provides ideal conditions for natural harbors and ports.

key_concepts.explanation: Shallow lagoon lakes found primarily on the Kerala coast. They are highly significant for fishing, inland navigation, and tourism.
Due to steep gradients, west-flowing rivers like Narmada and Tapi do not form deltas. Instead, they flow swiftly into the sea, forming deep estuaries at their mouths.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The northern subdivision of the western coastal plain, characterized by highly indented coastlines.
The central subdivision of the western coastal plain, rich in iron ore export facilities like New Mangalore port.
The southern subdivision of the western coastal plain. Famous for its backwaters (kayals) like Vembanad Lake.

important_facts.fact: The Western Coastal Plains are significantly narrower and more indented compared to the Eastern Coastal Plains.

sections.title: Eastern Coastal Plains
sections.description: Located between the Eastern Ghats and the Bay of Bengal, these plains are broader and are an example of an emergent coast, characterized by well-developed river deltas.

key_concepts.explanation: Major east-flowing rivers such as the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna, and Cauvery deposit massive amounts of silt at their mouths, creating extensive and highly fertile deltaic plains.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Coast of Odisha and Northern Andhra Pradesh
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The northern part of the eastern coastal plain, largely formed by the Mahanadi and Godavari river systems.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Coast of Southern Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The southern part of the eastern coastal plain. It uniquely receives heavy rainfall during the winter season from the North-East (Retreating) Monsoon.

important_facts.fact: Chilika Lake, located on the Odisha coast south of the Mahanadi delta, is the largest brackish water lake in India.

sections.title: Andaman and Nicobar Islands
sections.description: An archipelago of 572 islands in the Bay of Bengal. These islands are primarily of tectonic and volcanic origin, considered to be an elevated portion of submarine mountains (an extension of Myanmar's Arakan Yoma).

key_concepts.explanation: A narrow strait of water lying on the 10-degree north latitude that separates the Andaman Islands in the north from the Nicobar Islands in the south.

geographical_data.key_characteristics: The highest peak of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, standing at an elevation of 732 meters.
It is the only confirmed active volcano in India, as well as in the entire South Asian region.

important_facts.fact: Indira Point, located on the Great Nicobar Island, is the southernmost point of the Indian territory.

sections.title: Lakshadweep Islands
sections.description: Located in the Arabian Sea off the Malabar Coast, it is India's smallest Union Territory. The archipelago consists of 36 islands primarily formed entirely of coral deposits.

key_concepts.explanation: Ring-shaped coral reefs, islands, or series of islets. Lakshadweep islands are formed by the calcium carbonate skeletons of microscopic marine organisms known as coral polyps.

key_associations.extra_info: This maritime boundary separates the island nation of Maldives from Minicoy (the southernmost island of Lakshadweep).
This channel separates Minicoy Island from the rest of the Lakshadweep islands to the north.

important_facts.fact: Kavaratti is the administrative capital of Lakshadweep, and Pitti Island, which is uninhabited, has a famous bird sanctuary.

sections.title: Major Coastal Water Bodies
sections.description: The Indian coastline features several prominent lagoons and straits that hold immense ecological, geographical, and strategic importance.

geographical_data.location_or_origin: Border of Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu
geographical_data.key_characteristics: The second-largest brackish water lagoon in India. The barrier island of Sriharikota, which houses the Satish Dhawan Space Centre, separates it from the Bay of Bengal.
The longest lake in India and the largest lake in the state of Kerala. It is renowned for hosting the annual Nehru Trophy Snake Boat Race.

key_associations.extra_info: A strait that connects the Bay of Bengal in the northeast with the Palk Bay and separates the Indian state of Tamil Nadu from the island nation of Sri Lanka.
